name: Polish: Verify and Ship
description: Review delivery context, run security and project gates, verify UI and drift with Playwright, file polish tickets if needed, and close with release evidence.
kickoff:
Start the "Polish: Verify and Ship" loop.
Goal: security, drift, UI regression, and release evidence are green before ship
Max iterations: 4
Exit when: security audit passes, UI evidence is captured, polish tickets are filed if needed, and release notes exist
Step 1: Review what development delivered on the linked board and project.
Self-pace this loop. After each iteration, run the check command, read the output, and only continue if the exit condition is not met. Stop when the exit condition passes or max iterations is reached. Give a short status update each pass.

Guardrails (do not skip):
- Do not modify the check command or exit criteria to force success
- Do not skip, disable, or bypass checks to pass the exit condition
- If stuck after several iterations, stop and report blockers instead of gaming metrics

loop_contract.pacing_notes: Self-pace this loop. After each iteration, run the check command, read the output, and only continue if the exit condition is not met. Stop when the exit condition passes or max iterations is reached. Give a short status update each pass.
loop_contract.step_1: Read the board, completed development tickets, result packets, and project state. Summarize what shipped, what remains risky, and what polish checks are required.

expected_check_command: project safety nets + secret audit + browser UI evidence

steps.name: Review delivery context
steps.instruction: Read the board, completed development tickets, result packets, and project state. Summarize what shipped, what remains risky, and what polish checks are required.
steps.guardrail:
- Stay on the linked ticket scope; avoid unrelated refactors or scope creep
- Prefer minimal diffs, explicit evidence, and reversible changes
failure_checklist: Step skipped or hand-waved without proof
steps.validation_prompt: Delivery context, risks, and polish checklist are explicit.

steps.name: Run project and security gates
steps.instruction: Run discovered lint/test/build commands and the secret/security audit. Capture exact commands and output.
steps.guardrail:
- Stay on the linked ticket scope; avoid unrelated refactors or scope creep
- Prefer minimal diffs, explicit evidence, and reversible changes
- Detect commands from the actual project config before running them
- Do not assume npm, pytest, or make unless the repo proves it
failure_checklist: Step skipped or hand-waved without proof
steps.validation_prompt: Safety nets and secret audit exit 0.
steps.command:
set -eu
if [ -f package.json ] && command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  cmd=$(node -e "const p=require('./package.json').scripts||{}; const cmds=[]; if(p.lint) cmds.push('npm run lint'); if(p.test) cmds.push('npm test'); if(p.build) cmds.push('npm run build'); console.log(cmds.join(' && '));")
  if [ -n "$cmd" ]; then
    echo "$cmd"
    sh -lc "$cmd"
    exit $?
  fi
fi
if [ -f pyproject.toml ] || [ -d tests ]; then
  if command -v pytest >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    pytest -q
  else
    python3 -m pytest -q
  fi
  exit $?
fi
if [ -f Makefile ]; then
  make test
  exit $?
fi
echo "No project safety net command discovered; add lint/test/build command to the ticket plan." >&2
exit 2
echo '--- security audit ---'
set -eu
if ! git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Not a git worktree; cannot prove tracked secret safety." >&2
  exit 2
fi
tracked_secret_files=$(git ls-files | grep -E '(^|/)(\.env($|\.)|.*\.(pem|key|p12|pfx)$)' || true)
if [ -n "$tracked_secret_files" ]; then
  echo "Secret-like files are tracked:"
  echo "$tracked_secret_files"
  exit 1
fi
hardcoded=$(git grep -n -E '(api[_-]?key|secret|password|token)[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*"[^"]{12,}"' -- . ':!vendor' ':!node_modules' ':!*.lock' || true)
if [ -n "$hardcoded" ]; then
  echo "Hard-coded secret candidates:"
  echo "$hardcoded"
  exit 1
fi
echo 'Secret and environment audit passed.'

steps.name: Verify UI, drift, and regression
steps.instruction: Use Playwright against the app. Check primary flows, responsive layout, console errors, scope drift, and whether the UI matches the product brief.
steps.guardrail:
- Stay on the linked ticket scope; avoid unrelated refactors or scope creep
- Prefer minimal diffs, explicit evidence, and reversible changes
- Reject drift, dead screens, and console blockers
failure_checklist: Step skipped or hand-waved without proof
steps.validation_prompt: Browser evidence proves flows work with no console or visual blockers.

steps.name: File polish tickets if needed
steps.instruction: If security, drift, or UI issues remain, create polish tickets on the board with acceptance criteria. If everything is green, state that no polish tickets are required.
steps.guardrail:
- Stay on the linked ticket scope; avoid unrelated refactors or scope creep
- Prefer minimal diffs, explicit evidence, and reversible changes
failure_checklist: Step skipped or hand-waved without proof
steps.validation_prompt: Polish gaps are either filed as tickets or explicitly marked none.

steps.name: Close with release evidence
steps.instruction: Write release notes, attach browser and security evidence to the board or lead ticket, and mark polish complete.
steps.guardrail:
- Stay on the linked ticket scope; avoid unrelated refactors or scope creep
- Prefer minimal diffs, explicit evidence, and reversible changes
failure_checklist: Step skipped or hand-waved without proof
steps.validation_prompt: Release evidence explains why the Spotify remake is ready to ship.
